reviews.notes: Read the single pinned artifact in full (477 bytes, hash 4f3cd4a60ef1571fe310bfdca271b37b8ad972a6228f12ff3769af8cc28b33c0). It is a plan, not a report of executed results, so both criteria are assessed against the stated design. Criterion 1 fails: the comparison is deliberately unmatched, with A trained on 100 examples and B evaluated on a different set of 20 harder examples, and no shared metric, baseline, or example set is specified. Criterion 2 fails: the plan states A's accuracy is reported on the same 100 examples used for training, giving zero held-out data, and explicitly says "Do not use a held-out test set." The artifact self-identifies with the marker DESIGN-UNMATCHED-TRAIN100-TEST20, which matches the observed content. Because the defect is the experimental design itself (no held-out data and non-comparable conditions), no execution-time or reporting repair can yield a valid conclusion; the work must return to the planning stage to define matched conditions and a proper held-out split. No other artifacts were pinned, so no further evidence was available to consult.

reviews.notes: Read review.get, then artifact.read on both pinned artifacts in full. Plan artifact (marker PLAN-MATCHED-HELDOUT100) requires the same 100 held-out examples for A and B with accuracy = correct/100, retaining all examples including errors: met. Execution artifact (marker RUN-CORRECT80-WRONG20-DENOM100) records A at 80 correct and 20 incorrect, then removes the 20 errors and reports 80/80=100%, while B uses 75/100=75%; the retained counts imply A is 80/100=80%. That violates the full-100 denominator and the retain-all-examples rule: not_met. The report itself states the plan is usable but the execution/report must be repaired. Design is valid, so the destination is running for repair, not planned.
